articles.title: Blind since birth, he plays twenty instruments and sings in ten languages
articles.deck: Bhaskar Rao sat in the corner of a room until he was ten. Then a pastor asked whether he wanted to go to school. He talks about the music diplomas, the electronics degree, and why he took up music to prove a point.

hero.alt: Bhaskar Rao playing a bamboo flute against a brick wall, wearing dark glasses

interviewMeta.subject: V. Bhaskar Rao
interviewMeta.subjectBio: A music composer for the Christian organisation VishwaVani, a keyboard tutor, and an electronics engineer who repairs church instruments. He holds an MA in flute.

archiveMeta.editNote: First published as Talent Search #4. Reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the answers are his, unchanged.

body.v: Bhaskar Rao was born blind, and is capable of doing any work a sighted person does. He is a musician and composer several times over, and he holds a diploma in electronics and can work on electronic equipment. Despite a full schedule he gave us his time, his testimony and a good deal of encouragement.

Rather than dwelling on the sight he lacked, he built on the senses and the health he had, and made himself an educated, well-rounded man who has reached a great many people — through his life, and through his music ministry. He has fun wherever he goes. He is easy to get along with, children gather round him, and he is happy to answer any question they have about his blindness. Because of him a good many people have come to Jesus, and that is what keeps him going. He has inspired blind and sighted people alike to work with what they have rather than what they do not.
“What are the talents you have?”
5Talents: Hello Mr Bhaskar. Greetings from 5Talents — how are you?
Praise the Lord. Let all the glory be to Him. Whatever I am today is because of Him.
5Talents: What are the talents you have?

I did a diploma in music — western, Carnatic and Hindustani — and an MA specialising in flute. I can play the keyboard, trumpet, saxophone, clarinet, guitar, tabla, mridangam and mouth organ. I speak and sing in ten languages. I can create more than three hundred mimicry voices. I completed my electronic engineering and can replace microchip ICs with the LED balls of the electronics.
5Talents: That is amazing. Being a blind person, how is it possible?
People who have vision think blind people are useless and not capable of doing any work. To overcome that opinion I decided to take a step that would prove them wrong.

My father died when I was five. Until I was ten I just sat in a corner of a room like a doll, useless. But I was listening to music, which was the only source of knowledge and the only pleasant thing I had. I got a strong desire to learn music, and to learn the world.

One day a pastor met me and asked whether I wanted to study at a school. I agreed. He enrolled me at the Lutheran School for the Blind at Guntur, and my life changed from a hopeless blind boy into a transformed new person. I learned Braille — a system of raised dots you read by touch. I did six years of a diploma in music, and after that the electronic engineering.
Bhaskar Rao has mastered twenty musical instruments, and he speaks and sings in ten languages.
“I thought Jesus was a lower-caste god”
5Talents: When did you receive Jesus Christ as your personal saviour?

Surprisingly, even though I studied in a Christian school, I hated Christians. I was brought up in an upper-caste family where we worshipped many gods and goddesses, so I thought Jesus was a lower-caste god — why should I accept this god?

But one day I realised I had no relationship with the gods I had worshipped. The priest at the temple did not even know me, and this pastor cared about me and about my life. As I learned more about Jesus Christ and His sacrifice for my sins and for the sin of the whole world, I began to put my faith in Him and to believe Him as the only God. I also learned that Jesus Christ is the resurrection, and that He has resurrection power, which no other man or god or goddess has. I accepted Him as my personal saviour and Lord and submitted my life to Him.

Today I say proudly that a blind man like me is capable of doing everything, because I have achieved it in my life through Jesus Christ. It is not me who does those things — it is God who works in me.
The work
5Talents: How do you use your talents to glorify Jesus?

I am currently a music composer for a Christian organisation, VishwaVani. I attend musical programmes and gospel meetings to sing and play for the Lord. I am especially concerned about young people, and I am mostly invited to speak among them and encourage them. I am a professional keyboard tutor for western music, and students come to me for music and vocals. I repair keyboards of any brand — church instruments are especially often brought to me.
5Talents: How do you encourage people who have not discovered their talents, or who are discouraged by others?

Knowing your talent is itself a specialty. And having discovered it, a person will use it for the Lord’s kingdom only after they surrender their life to Christ. Without giving one’s life to God, a person will never think to use their talent for God, because in worldly terms you can earn a lot of money through a talent.

Dear readers, if you are handicapped, do not despair and do not be discouraged. Take a step towards Jesus and have faith in Him. He will transform your life to great heights as He has done in mine. Today I am a transformed Bhaskar Rao, and God has blessed me with a good wife, children and a standing in society.
It has been twenty-seven years now. I am using all these talents for His kingdom and His glory, and I will continue to the end.

articles.title: In nine years of ministry I have watched leaders quietly become puppets
articles.deck: The manager who never leaves the chair. The supreme leader who decides by preference. And Elijah, who went from calling down fire to lying under a tree asking to die.

archiveMeta.editNote: Lightly edited for reading order and typographical errors.

body.v: In nine years of ministry I have seen Christian ministry leaders fall repeatedly into two categories. A prophet is someone who says what God is saying and does what God is doing. Against that stands the puppet.
Puppets have someone, or something, else pulling the strings of their life.

Sometimes it is the squeaky wheel. In a Christian organisation it is the managers who never want to leave their chairs, complaining constantly about preferences. They choose which staff they want to work with, whom they can control, and how to extract work from them while keeping a lid on their talents.

Some managers hold their position for years. How? When you are talented, innovative, creative, with the makings of a leader, they suppress your conduct, pull you down and keep you in your place. They take the credit for the good things employees do and redirect the blame when something goes wrong. That is a glance at the Christian workplace today.
So who is the puppet?
The supreme leader of the organisation — the one who makes decisions on a manager’s preferences, or on his own.

Leaders need to lead out of principle, not preference. Leaders need to programme services by principle, not preference. If you let the people with the preferences make the rules, you are not only a puppet — biblically you have become a judge, asking God to move off His throne so you can sit there instead.
Others allow controlling personalities, or the spirit of Jezebel, to lead their life and their ministry.
We have all struggled between the role of prophet and puppet at times.
Elijah under the tree

One of the clearest cases in the Bible is Elijah. On the mountaintop he was God’s man, calling down fire from heaven and proving to his generation that God was God. Then he hears that Jezebel is after him. He went from prophet to puppet just like that — running for his life, falling under a tree, praying that he would die.

Biblical leadership includes direction from above. David says: “He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters… He guides me in the paths of righteousness.” (Psalm 23:2–3) The world assumes people will automatically know the best direction by following their feelings. God rejects that and puts forward leadership and authority instead. In His view we often need outside direction on which way to go.
Biblical guidance matters in ministry, but we are still left to apply biblical teaching area by area, and those are often judgment calls that need wisdom and experience.
Success is a bad teacher

Success in ministry can lead to the wrong conclusions. We may decide that because we succeeded, our methods must have been especially correct. Meanwhile the success may be the result of something else entirely, and we usually have no way of knowing until we fail using those same miracle methods.

Failure throws us into amazement and disillusionment, and that confused state of mind is exactly what God needs in order to bring us out of an ego-driven way of seeing things. Only then can we listen to new ideas, to new explanations of past success, and think originally about the future.
We have to cut ourselves free from the people, and the preferences, that control and manipulate us when we make decisions. We must be willing to lead, and to be the prophet, not the puppet.

articles.title: Every job in a king’s palace has a match in the church
articles.deck: Soldiers, watchmen, messengers, potters, musicians, gardeners, administrators. A theology lecturer runs the whole staff list and asks who you are on it.

archiveMeta.editNote: Lightly edited for reading order and typographical errors. The scripture references are the author’s.

body.v: A king needs efficient workers for the special tasks of the palace. The worker has to be sincere, honest and hard-working. Every worker has his own duties and responsibilities. What follows are some of the king’s men appointed to perform theirs in the royal palace — set against the kingdom of God, where every one of us has a responsibility to take up in His palace.
“…He is Lord of lords and King of kings — and with him will be his called, chosen and faithful followers.” (Revelation 17:14)
Soldiers — pastors

“Endure hardship with us like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.” (2 Timothy 2:3) They work for the king and fight for the king to extend the kingdom, and they guard the palace day and night. Pastors do the same: they work for the king, fight to establish His kingdom on earth, and guard His palace around the clock. That palace is called the church.
Watchmen — prayer warriors

“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.” (Ezekiel 3:17) Watchmen are as old as cities, robbers and wars. Jerusalem and other cities kept regular guards night and day. Prayer warriors are watchmen. They guard the palace by praying — for individuals, for families, for the sick, and for salvation.
Messengers — evangelists

“…which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven.” (1 Peter 1:12) Messengers bring and carry news for the king, and they communicate between the people and the king. Evangelists stand in that place on this earth. The regular Hebrew word for messenger is mal’akh, the Greek aggelos — which may mean a human messenger or a messenger of God, an angel.
Potters — the women’s fellowship

“These were the potters and those who dwell at Netaim and Gederah; there they dwelt with the king for his work.” (1 Chronicles 4:23) Potters prepare vessels for the king’s use. They were probably brick makers, and perhaps potters too, living on low ground and working the clay dug up in forming the fences of the palace into pots and bricks. The women’s fellowship prepares the church — its children, its young people, its elders and its believers — to be used.
Musicians — worship leaders

“…I acquired men and women singers, and a harem as well — the delights of the heart of man.” (Ecclesiastes 2:8) Musicians play and sing for the king in his palace, and their job is to please him and to glorify him. Worship leaders lead the choir in praise and worship, magnify the Lord for the miracles He has done, and connect the congregation to heaven in singing.
Gardeners — Sunday school teachers

“They made me keeper of the vineyards.” (Song of Songs 1:6) The gardener plants the varieties of plants, herbs and crops in the king’s garden, and his duty is to see that they are well rooted and watered and that the ground is fertilised. The Sunday school teacher is the gardener and the students are the plants; the children should be nurtured in the word of God and in prayer.
Administrators — church elders

“…the young men without any physical defect, handsome, showing aptitude for every kind of learning, well informed, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace.” (Daniel 1:4) Administrators govern the other workers in the palace. They assist the king, directing or managing affairs, whether civil, judicial, political or ecclesiastical. Church elders manage the affairs of the church and support the pastor in managing the congregation.
Working for the king

The workers work for the king to get a reward, and to receive his blessing. The king’s workers carry the same honour and respect the king has. Our God is the King of kings, who not only cares for His workers but loves them, and who is at this moment preparing a place for them in His kingdom.

Those who work in the king’s palace will never know scarcity. They are given all the facilities the king possesses. In 1 Kings 4:22–23 we read of the thousands of King Solomon’s workers, given the best food and living a royal life. The king always meets the physical, spiritual and social needs of a worker.
His palace needs creative and hard workers. The place is not for lazy people.

There is a need for workers in the kingdom of God. The King has called all of us into His palace, and there is much to do. Are you ready to join the crew? Let us get involved in the church of God — the king’s palace is nothing but the church. Let us be workers of the church, and work for the king and live for the king.
